questions.question:
A 2 meter long scale with least count of 0.2 cm is used to measure the locations of objects on an optical bench. While measuring the focal length of a convex lens, the object pin and the convex lens are placed at 80 cm mark and 1 m mark respectively. The image of the object pin on the other side of lens coincides with image pin that is kept at 180 cm mark. The % error in the estimation of focal length is:

[JEE Main 2023, 6 Apr (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
Least count is \(0.2 \mathrm{~cm}\)
\[
\begin{aligned}
& u=(100 \pm 0.2)-(80 \pm 0.2)=(20 \pm 0.4) \mathrm{cm} \\
& v=(180 \pm 0.2)-(100 \pm 0.2)=(80 \pm 0.4) \mathrm{cm}
\end{aligned}
\]

From lens formula,
\[
\begin{aligned}
& \frac{1}{f}=\frac{1}{v}-\frac{1}{u} \Rightarrow \frac{1}{f}=\frac{1}{80}-\frac{1}{-20}=\frac{-20-80}{-1600} \\
& f=16 \mathrm{~cm}
\end{aligned}
\]

Also \(\frac{\Delta f}{f^2}=\frac{\Delta v}{v^2}+\frac{\Delta u}{u^2}\)
\[
\begin{aligned}
& \therefore \frac{\Delta f}{f} \times 100=\left(\frac{\Delta v}{v^2}+\frac{\Delta u}{u^2}\right) \times f \times 100 \\
& \Rightarrow \% f=\left(\frac{0.4}{400}+\frac{0.4}{6400}\right) \times 16 \times 100=1.70
\end{aligned}
\]

Maximum tension occurs at mean position.

\]

\[
\begin{aligned}
& \frac{1}{2} m v^2=m g l(1-\cos \theta) \Rightarrow \frac{m v^2}{l}=2 m g(1-\cos \theta) \\
& \therefore T=m g+2 m g(1-\cos \theta) \\

& \therefore x=99
\end{aligned}
\]

S1:A∩B=(1,∞)-N and S2:A∪B=(1,∞)

 

[JEE Main 2023, 6 Apr (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
Here, \([x]\) denotes the smallest integer greater than or equal to \(x\), that is,

\([x]=\lceil x\rceil\).

The function is

\(f(x)=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\lceil x\rceil-x}}\).

If \(x\in\mathbb Z\), then

\(\lceil x\rceil-x=0\).

Therefore, the denominator becomes zero, so integral values of \(x\) are not in the domain.

If \(x\notin\mathbb Z\), then

\(0<\lceil x\rceil-x<1\).

Hence, the domain is

\(A=\mathbb R-\mathbb Z\).

Let

\(t=\lceil x\rceil-x\).

As \(x\) varies over the non-integral real numbers, \(t\) takes every value in \((0,1)\).

Therefore,

\(f(x)=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt t}\),

where

\(0<t<1\).

Hence,

\(f(x)>1\).

Also, every value greater than \(1\) can be obtained.

Therefore, the range is

\(B=(1,\infty)\).

Thus,

\(A\cap B=(1,\infty)-\mathbb N\).

Hence, statement \((S_1)\) is true.

However, \(A\cup B\) contains non-integral real numbers less than or equal to \(1\).

Therefore,

\(A\cup B\ne(1,\infty)\).

Hence, statement \((S_2)\) is false.

Therefore, only \((S_1)\) is true.

\(z=x+iy\)

\(u=\operatorname{Re}(z^2)=x^2-y^2\).

Also,

\(\operatorname{Re}(\overline z)=x\).

Therefore, the two given equations become

\(au+bx=a\)

and

\(bu+ax=b\).

Writing them in a more useful form,

\(a(u-1)+bx=0\)

and

\(b(u-1)+ax=0\).

Multiplying the first equation by \(a\),

\(a^2(u-1)+abx=0\).

Multiplying the second equation by \(b\),

\(b^2(u-1)+abx=0\).

Subtracting,

\((a^2-b^2)(u-1)=0\).

Since

\(a\ne\pm b\),

\(a^2-b^2\ne0\).

Hence,

\(u=1\).

Now multiply

\(a(u-1)+bx=0\)

by \(b\), and

\(b(u-1)+ax=0\)

by \(a\). We get

\(ab(u-1)+b^2x=0\)

and

\(ab(u-1)+a^2x=0\).

Subtracting,

\((b^2-a^2)x=0\).

Again,

\(a^2\ne b^2\),

so

\(x=0\).

But

\(u=x^2-y^2=1\).

Using \(x=0\),

\(-y^2=1\),

which has no real value of \(y\).

Therefore, there is no complex number \(z=x+iy\) satisfying both equations.

Hence,

\(X=\varnothing\),

so the number of elements in \(X\) is \(0\).

Therefore, the correct option is C.

Let \(f(x)=x^5-20x^3+50x+2\).

The points where the curve crosses the \(x\)-axis are the

real roots of \(f(x)=0\) at which the sign of \(f(x)\) changes.

Here \(f(-5)=(-5)^5-20(-5)^3+50(-5)+2=-3125+2500-250+2=-873<0\).

Also \(f(-4)=(-4)^5-20(-4)^3+50(-4)+2=-1024+1280-200+2=58>0\).

Therefore, one real root lies in \((-5,-4)\).

Also \(f(-2)=(-2)^5-20(-2)^3+50(-2)+2=-32+160-100+2=30>0\).

and \(f(-1)=(-1)^5-20(-1)^3+50(-1)+2=-1+20-50+2=-29<0\).

Therefore, one real root lies in \((-2,-1)\).

We have \(f(-1)=-29<0\) and \(f(0)=2>0\).

Therefore, one real root lies in \((-1,0)\).

Again \(f(1)=1-20+50+2=33>0\).

and \(f(2)=32-160+100+2=-26<0\).

Therefore, one real root lies in \((1,2)\).

Now \(f(4)=1024-1280+200+2=-54<0\).

and \(f(5)=3125-2500+250+2=877>0\).

Therefore, one real root lies in \((4,5)\).

The five intervals \((-5,-4)\), \((-2,-1)\), \((-1,0)\), \((1,2)\), and \((4,5)\) are mutually disjoint.

Hence, \(f(x)=0\) has at least five distinct real roots.

Since \(f(x)\) is a polynomial of degree \(5\),

it cannot have more than five real roots.

Therefore, \(f(x)=0\) has exactly five distinct real roots.

The sign of \(f(x)\) changes across each of these roots,

so the curve crosses the \(x\)-axis at all five points.
